question: Should core add a backward-compatible deterministic acknowledgment-reaction pool, permit a model-driven contextual chooser, or retain the existing singular reaction contract?
rationale: The choice defines a new cross-channel config and runtime contract with materially different latency, predictability, compatibility, and plugin-boundary tradeoffs; source inspection cannot determine the intended product behavior.

options.title: Deterministic configured pool
options.body: Preserve `ackReaction` and add an optional pool selected without another model call, with stable channel-aware fallback behavior.

options.title: Model-driven contextual selection
options.body: Let a model choose from an allowed pool before acknowledgment, accepting extra latency, cost, and failure handling.

options.title: Keep one reaction
options.body: Retain the current singular contract and close the request rather than expand core configuration and channel policy.

recommendation.title: Deterministic configured pool
recommendation.body: Preserve `ackReaction` and add an optional pool selected without another model call, with stable channel-aware fallback behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This person already supplied product-direction engagement on the exact request and asked for a backward-compatible core/channel design.
